name: Vantage Data Centers colocation: published rack power-density tiers (8.3 kW avg / 20 kW air-cooled / 50 kW+ liquid-to-rack)
region: North America, EMEA and APAC (nearly 1.5 GW+ of potential IT power across all three)
price_basis: NO FIGURE IS PUBLISHED. Vantage prices colocation by quote only - there is no per-rack-month, per-kW-month or per-GPU-hour rate on any public page. This is itself a finding: colo power economics are not comparable across providers without a quote, so this record carries the density limits (which ARE published) rather than an invented price.
notes: ONE OF THE FEWEST COLOS THAT PUBLISHES ITS PER-RACK POWER LIMITS AT ALL, which makes it the reference point for the colo half of this slice. Verbatim from their Power features page: standard data module supports 'an average of 8.3kW of power to each rack'; 'customers have the flexibility to deploy up to 20kW racks with traditional air-cooled technology and more than 50kW racks using liquid to rack cooling solutions'; campus footprints 'up to 300 watts per square foot'; each standard data module 'includes 4MW of IT capacity'; annualized PUE under 1.3 targeting low 1.2. Redundancy is a '5 to make 4' distributed redundant weave architecture equating to N+1 for concurrent maintainability, with 2.75MW diesel gensets on 5,000-gallon belly tanks sized to carry full IT load for 24 hours. Their own Highlights project '8.3kW to the rack on average, projecting 11kW+ in near future' - i.e. even the colo operator is telling you the average rack is not the interesting number. THE THREE TIERS ARE THE WHOLE ARGUMENT: 8.3 kW avg (typical colo), 20 kW air-cooled ceiling, 50 kW+ only with liquid to rack. Map a rack-level AI system onto that: a DGX H100 at 10.2 kW max fits tier 1-2 today; an 8-GPU HGX B200 node at roughly 8-10 kW of IT load plus PSU overhead fits tier 2; a GB200 NVL72 at ~120 kW is 14x their average rack and 6x their air-cooled ceiling, and needs a tier that does not exist in this facility. NOTE the accelerator_ids above list GB200 NVL72 and B200 as REACHABLE IN PRINCIPLE via the 50 kW+ liquid tier, not as confirmed inventory - Vantage publishes capacity, not SKUs, and the companion cooling page (supply/colo-vantage-liquid-to-rack-not-to-chip) makes clear their liquid tier is liquid-to-the-RACK, which is not the same plumbing as the in-rack cold-plate loop a GB200 NVL72 needs.
